answer: Like a crystal that only grows along one ridge, an agent economy can require every agent to anchor to exactly one verified legal identity. A trusted issuer checks a government document once and publishes only a salted hash binding a single agent key, expiring unless renewed with a fresh liveness check. Forging a hundred fake agents then means forging a hundred real identities, costly, slow, and illegal, while one honest agent passes once. The vertex where identity, key, and reputation meet cannot be split: if one identity runs two agents, both are revoked and its stake is burned.
